scope.definition_policy: Every regulatory node includes a plain, source-grounded definition assembled from the retained proposition or related propositions.
scope.consolidation_policy: Requirements from the same primary legal provision or shared source clause are retained as nested requirements instead of separate graph nodes.

rules.rule_name: APM Elizabeth weekday gate opening time
rules.definition: APM Terminals Elizabeth gates open Monday through Friday at 6:00 a.m.

structured_values.measurement_scope: APM Elizabeth gates Monday through Friday

rules.rule_name: APM Elizabeth standard gate cutoff time
rules.definition: APM Terminals Elizabeth lists a 4:00 p.m. gate cutoff for empties, the PND 921 Delancey St. empty depot, dry loads, and reefer loads. APM Terminals Elizabeth lists a 3:30 p.m. gate cutoff for Out-of-Gauge (OOG) loads.
source_sections: Hours of Operation cutoff table, page 1

rules.rule_name: APM Elizabeth weekend and holiday hours may vary
rules.definition: APM Terminals Elizabeth states that weekend gate hours may vary. APM Terminals Elizabeth states that holiday gate hours may vary.

rules.rule_name: APM Elizabeth TERMPoint appointment system
rules.definition: APM Terminals Elizabeth uses TERMPoint as the truck appointment system for managing terminal truck appointments.

rules.rule_name: TERMPoint import and export appointment scheduling
rules.definition: TERMPoint supports requests for import appointments. TERMPoint supports requests for export appointments. TERMPoint supports simultaneous scheduling of an import appointment and an export appointment.

rules.rule_name: APM appointment availability may change with terminal closures
rules.definition: Appointment availability may change when APM Terminals Elizabeth is closed.

rules.rule_name: Marine terminal appointment prior to gate arrival
rules.definition: If visiting an applicable marine terminal, the trucker should have an appointment before arriving at the gate.
source_sections: General Information — What to Have Prior to Arriving at Gate, page 3

rules.rule_name: Driver license, TWIC, and SeaLink required before gate arrival
rules.definition: The PANYNJ truckers guide recommends that a trucker have a valid driver license before arriving at a marine-terminal gate. The PANYNJ truckers guide recommends that a trucker have a valid TWIC before arriving at a marine-terminal gate. The PANYNJ truckers guide recommends that a trucker have valid SeaLink identification before arriving at a marine-terminal gate.
source_sections: General Information — What to Have Prior to Arriving at Gate, page 3

rules.rule_name: TWIC required for secure or restricted maritime facility access
rules.definition: TWIC is required by federal law for workers, including drayage truck drivers, who need access to secure or restricted areas of maritime facilities.

rules.rule_name: Original TWIC must be presented for inspection
rules.definition: The original TWIC must be presented for inspection when requesting unescorted access to a secure or restricted area of a marine terminal or vessel.
source_sections: TWIC Care and Handling Instructions, page 3

rules.rule_name: SeaLink mandatory for port truckers
rules.definition: SeaLink is the Port Authority's uniform truck driver identification system and is mandatory for all truckers doing business at the Port of New York and New Jersey.

rules.rule_name: SeaLink users must also have TWIC
rules.definition: Anyone with SeaLink identification must also have a TWIC, and the TWIC must be registered with the Port Authority at the Truck Service Center.

rules.rule_name: Class 8 drayage trucks must be registered in DTR and have RFID
rules.definition: A Class 8 drayage truck seeking entry to a Port of New York and New Jersey marine terminal must be registered in the Drayage Truck Registry.

rules.rule_name: No RFID tag means no entry
rules.definition: The guidebook states: no tag, no entry. Trucks with 1998 and older engine models are prohibited and will be denied access to port terminals in the Port of New York and New Jersey. Only drayage trucks equipped with engines meeting or exceeding federal EPA on-road emission standards for 2014 model year heavy-duty diesel-fueled engines are permitted to register in the DTR via PortTruckPass.

rules.rule_name: One RFID tag per unique vehicle
rules.definition: Each unique vehicle identified by VIN and license plate may be associated with only one RFID tag in the Drayage Truck Registry.

rules.rule_name: DTR access denial reasons
rules.definition: A truck may be denied marine-terminal entry when it is not found in the Drayage Truck Registry. A truck may be denied marine-terminal entry when it has not been approved for port entry. A truck may be denied marine-terminal entry when it has a pre-1999 engine.

rules.rule_name: UIIA registration and insurance/credit documentation before gate arrival
rules.definition: The PANYNJ truckers guide recommends that a trucking company have proof of UIIA registration before gate arrival. The PANYNJ truckers guide recommends that a trucking company have evidence of valid insurance with the steamship line being hauled for before gate arrival. The PANYNJ truckers guide recommends that a trucking company have valid credit with the steamship line being hauled for before gate arrival.
source_sections: General Information — What to Have Prior to Arriving at Gate, page 3

rules.rule_name: Large-truck route hierarchy in New Jersey
rules.definition: New Jersey establishes a roadway hierarchy for double-trailer truck combinations and 102-inch-wide standard trucks: National Network, New Jersey Access Network, and other local unrestricted roadways.

rules.rule_name: Large-truck National Network trip-completion duty
rules.definition: Double-trailer truck combinations and 102-inch-wide standard trucks must complete trips using the National Network except as otherwise provided in N.J.A.C. 16:32.

rules.rule_name: Local unrestricted roadways only as necessary for terminal access
rules.definition: A covered large truck may use a local unrestricted roadway only as necessary to access a terminal located on that roadway.

rules.rule_name: Other state, county, and municipal restrictions still apply
rules.definition: N.J.A.C. 16:32 does not supersede other state rules, municipal ordinances, or county resolutions that may restrict truck movements, including posted weight limits or local truck-route restrictions.

rules.rule_name: NJ Route 81 is part of the National Network near Elizabeth
rules.definition: NJ Route 81 from I-95 in Elizabeth to US 1 at Newark Airport is designated as part of the National Network for double-trailer truck combinations and 102-inch-wide standard trucks.

structured_values.measurement_scope: vehicle class covered by the NJ Route 81 National Network designation

rules.rule_name: Terminal access documentation may demonstrate compliant routing
rules.definition: When accessing terminals off the National Network, drivers may use documentation such as a bill of lading, delivery receipt, shipping order, manifest, log book, route map, written route description, or dispatcher confirmation to demonstrate compliant terminal-access routing.

rules.rule_name: Commercial vehicle width limit depends on route designation
rules.definition: A commercial vehicle is limited to 96 inches in width on a route that is neither a National Network route nor a New Jersey Access Route.

rules.rule_name: Commercial vehicle height limit
rules.definition: The maximum height for a commercial vehicle or combination of vehicles, including load, is 13 feet 6 inches unless otherwise identified.

structured_values.measurement_scope: commercial vehicle or vehicle combination including load

rules.rule_name: Trailer length depends on network/access-route status
rules.definition: A trailer or semitrailer may be 53 feet long on the National Network and access routes, subject to the guide's configuration conditions.

structured_values.measurement_scope: National Network and access routes under stated configuration conditions

rules.rule_name: OS/OW permit required when size or weight limits are exceeded
rules.definition: A vehicle or vehicle combination transporting a load that exceeds New Jersey size or weight limitations requires a special permit to move on public roads, streets, highways, or public/quasi-public property in the state.
source_sections: Legal Size and Weight Limits, page 12; FAQ pages 8-9

rules.rule_name: New Jersey permit validity excludes some toll facilities without approval
rules.definition: New Jersey permits may not be used on the New Jersey Turnpike, Garden State Parkway south of Exit 105, or Atlantic City Expressway without express approval of the tolling authority.

rules.rule_name: TWIC applicants are subject to federal credentialing and security threat assessment rules
rules.definition: 49 CFR Part 1572 establishes credentialing and security threat assessment regulations for certain maritime and land transportation workers, including applicants obtaining or renewing a TWIC.

rules.rule_name: TSA may deny or invalidate TWIC based on security threat assessment standards
rules.definition: TSA may determine that a TWIC applicant poses a security threat based on a disqualifying criminal offense specified by 49 CFR Part 1572. TSA may immediately invalidate a TWIC when it determines that the holder poses an immediate threat under 49 CFR Part 1572.
source_sections: 49 CFR 1572.5 Standards for security threat assessments

rules.rule_name: Large-truck map provides route-designation reference for 102-inch truck network
rules.definition: The NJ Large Truck Map provides the route-designation reference used to identify National Network and NJ Access Route status for large trucks, including the 102-inch truck route network.

structured_values.measurement_scope: vehicle class depicted by the NJ Large Truck Map

rules.rule_name: APM published approach direction from US 1&9 South
rules.definition: APM's archived published directions for an approach from US 1&9 South instruct travelers to take the Elizabeth Seaport/North Avenue exit, follow North Avenue East to McLester Street, turn left, then turn right at Tripoli Street (the third traffic light); the named facility entrance is on the right. APM's archived published directions for an approach from New Jersey Turnpike Exit 13A instruct travelers to follow signs for Elizabeth Seaport/North Avenue, continue on North Avenue to McLester Street, turn left, then turn right at Tripoli Street (the third traffic light); the named facility entrance is on the right.

rules.rule_name: APM account supports terminal alerts and appointment services
rules.definition: An APMTerminals.com account enables subscription to terminal alerts.
source_sections: Create an Account and Terminal Alerts, PDF pages 4-5

rules.rule_name: TERMPoint covers import, export, and empty appointment requests
rules.definition: TERMPoint supports import appointment requests. TERMPoint supports export appointment requests. TERMPoint supports empty appointment requests. TERMPoint supports appointment-status monitoring. TERMPoint provides an import-container watch list. TERMPoint supports appointment swaps. TERMPoint displays driver information for appointment management. TERMPoint provides row-closure information.

rules.rule_name: TERMPoint Driver tab displays assigned-driver information
rules.definition: The TERMPoint Driver tab displays the driver assigned to an appointment. The TERMPoint Driver tab displays the assigned driver's safety-induction status. The archived APM source describes checking assigned-driver and safety-induction status before dispatch as a way to avoid turnaround at the inbound gate.

rules.rule_name: All APM Elizabeth gate moves require an appointment
rules.definition: The APM terminal-specific section states that all gate moves at APM Terminals Elizabeth require an appointment made through TERMPoint.
source_sections: APM Terminals, printed pages 18-19 / PDF page 11

rules.rule_name: APM safety induction required before terminal access
rules.definition: A driver must complete APM's online safety induction before accessing the terminal.
source_sections: APM Mandatory Trucker Training and Safety Advisory, printed pages 18 and 20 / PDF pages 11-12

rules.rule_name: APM appointment changes stop after inbound OCR
rules.definition: Appointments cannot be created, modified, or merged after the truck passes through inbound optical character recognition.
source_sections: APM Appointments, printed page 18 / PDF page 11

rules.rule_name: Import pickup information required before gate arrival
rules.definition: For an import pickup, the guide lists a freight release, container number, and bill-of-lading number as pre-arrival information. For an empty pickup, the guide lists a valid booking number, steamship line, and container length, height, and type as pre-arrival information. For an empty return or drop move, the guide lists the steamship line and container length, height, and type as pre-arrival information.
source_sections: What to Have Prior to Arriving at Gate, printed page 3 / PDF page 3

rules.rule_name: Export delivery or drop information required before gate arrival
rules.definition: For an export delivery or drop move, the guide lists a valid booking number, steamship line, and container dimensions/type, plus hazardous documentation, vehicle titles, over-dimensional measurements, or reefer commodity and temperature when applicable.
source_sections: What to Have Prior to Arriving at Gate, printed page 3 / PDF page 3

rules.rule_name: Container availability and holds should be cleared before dispatch
rules.definition: The PANYNJ truckers guide recommends confirming container availability before dispatch for an import pickup.
source_sections: Dos and Don'ts, printed pages 15-16 / PDF pages 9-10

rules.rule_name: Empty return destination must be checked before dispatch
rules.definition: The guide directs truckers to check the terminal website, mobile application, or TIPS for the current empty-return destination and acceptance information before returning an empty container.
source_sections: Dos and Don'ts and FAQs, printed pages 15 and 43 / PDF pages 9 and 23

rules.rule_name: Reefer temperature and genset requirements must be confirmed before dispatch
rules.definition: The guide directs truckers to confirm required reefer temperature and genset needs with the steamship line and terminal guidance before dispatch.
source_sections: Dos and Don'ts, printed pages 15-16 / PDF pages 9-10

rules.rule_name: APM roadability inspections depend on outbound equipment type
rules.definition: An outbound reefer must stop at APM's reefer roadability garage.
source_sections: APM Roadability, printed pages 18-19 / PDF page 11

rules.rule_name: APM terminal exit requires completion of outbound processing
rules.definition: APM requires a complete outbound ticket before terminal exit.
source_sections: APM Outgate Processing and Outbound Security, printed pages 19-20 / PDF pages 11-12

rules.rule_name: APM trouble conditions may trigger automatic void-out
rules.definition: Automatic void-out categories include container holds or status issues, driver or carrier status problems, SeaLink issues, hazardous-documentation problems, early/late/used/cancelled appointments, booking or cutoff issues, UIIA or carrier-agreement problems, and incomplete safety induction.
source_sections: APM Trouble Tickets, printed page 20 / PDF page 12

rules.rule_name: APM safety violations may suspend terminal access
rules.definition: A listed APM safety or transaction violation may deactivate a driver's SeaLink access.
source_sections: APM Trucker Violations and STEP Program, printed pages 22-23 / PDF page 13

rules.rule_name: PANYNJ marine-terminal highway size and weight limits
rules.definition: A containerized shipment on a PANYNJ marine-terminal highway may not exceed 128,000 pounds. The gross vehicle weight of a containerized shipment on a PANYNJ marine-terminal highway must not exceed the manufacturer's safe working loads. A vehicle exceeding 16 feet 3 inches in height or 11 feet in width requires approval from the Manager, Marine Terminals for shipment through the marine terminals.

rules.rule_name: PANYNJ terminal speed limits follow posted signs
rules.definition: A vehicle at a PANYNJ marine terminal must comply with speed limits shown on posted traffic signs. A vehicle may not be driven on a PANYNJ mooring facility at more than 12 miles per hour.

rules.rule_name: PANYNJ terminal parking follows authorization and posted signs
rules.definition: A vehicle at a PANYNJ marine terminal must park only in an authorized area.

rules.rule_name: Vehicles and operators require registration, licensing, and specified PANYNJ authorization
rules.definition: Motorized equipment used for waterborne-freight handling must have the state registration required by the tariff.

rules.rule_name: Traffic directions, lane markings, driver authorization, and registration govern terminal highways
rules.definition: Traffic on a PANYNJ terminal highway must obey lawful directions of Port Authority Police. The tariff prohibits transporting or parking listed explosive, flammable, corrosive, poisonous, compressed-gas, radioactive, and other hazardous materials on terminal highways at a time, place, manner, or condition likely to endanger persons or property.

rules.rule_name: DTR registration information must be maintained
rules.definition: A drayage truck seeking PANYNJ marine-terminal entry must be registered in the Drayage Truck Registry before entry. When information supplied for a registered drayage truck changes, the registration information must be amended through PortTruckPass within ten calendar days of the change.

rules.rule_name: 2014 EPA engine standard required to complete DTR registration
rules.definition: Beginning July 2, 2023 at 12:01 AM local time, only drayage trucks with engines meeting or exceeding federal EPA model-year 2014 heavy-duty diesel on-road emission standards may complete DTR registration.

rules.rule_name: PANYNJ tariff drayage access conditions beginning July 2, 2023
rules.definition: Beginning July 2, 2023 at 12:01 AM local time, the tariff states that a container terminal may not admit a drayage truck that cannot be verified as Drayage Truck Registry compliant. Beginning May 1, 2027 at 12:01 AM local time, the tariff states that a container terminal may not admit a drayage truck that cannot be verified as Drayage Truck Registry compliant. Beginning May 1, 2028 at 12:01 AM local time, the tariff states that a container terminal may not admit a drayage truck that cannot be verified as Drayage Truck Registry compliant. Beginning July 2, 2023 at 12:01 AM, a container terminal facility may not permit access to a drayage truck equipped with an engine of model year 1998 or older. Beginning July 2, 2023 at 12:01 AM, a container terminal facility may not permit access to a drayage truck that is not an Alternative Drayage Truck as defined in Subrule 34-1060. Beginning May 1, 2027 at 12:01 AM, a container terminal facility may not permit access to a drayage truck equipped with an engine of model year 1999 or older. Beginning May 1, 2027 at 12:01 AM, a container terminal facility may not permit access to a drayage truck that is not an Alternative Truck as defined in Subrule 34-1060. Beginning May 1, 2028 at 12:01 AM, a container terminal facility may not permit access to a drayage truck equipped with an engine of model year 2000 or older. Beginning May 1, 2028 at 12:01 AM, a container terminal facility may not permit access to a drayage truck that is not an Alternative Truck as defined in Subrule 34-1060.

rules.rule_name: Past-due PANYNJ accounts may result in denial of terminal use
rules.definition: PANYNJ reserves the right to deny terminal use until a past-due account is paid. A tariff invoice unpaid within 30 calendar days of the invoice date is subject to a fee of 0.8 percent on the outstanding balance and again every 15 days thereafter.

rules.rule_name: SeaLink transactions may carry registration and processing fees
rules.definition: SeaLink registration, replacement, renewal, and carrier-association transactions may carry the fees stated in the tariff.

rules.rule_name: PortTruckPass implements PANYNJ tariff truck-registration subrules
rules.definition: The PortTruckPass truck-registration service states that it implements Port Authority subrules published in FMC Schedule PA-10, including revisions.

rules.rule_name: TIPS provides common terminal information for cargo deployment decisions
rules.definition: TIPS is described as a common portal allowing motor carriers and cargo interests to manage and deploy resources when delivering or picking up cargo at the port.

rules.rule_name: New Jersey axle and gross-weight limits depend on axle configuration and route
rules.definition: New Jersey's general statutory maximum for a single axle is 22,400 pounds, subject to the cited exceptions and roadway context.

structured_values.measurement_scope: New Jersey general statutory single-axle maximum subject to cited exceptions
structured_values.conversion_method: pounds multiplied by 0.45359237; rounded to 0.1 kg

rules.rule_name: New Jersey annual ocean-borne container permit has configuration-specific weight limits
rules.definition: The New Jersey annual ocean-borne-container permit is limited to qualifying sealed ocean-borne containers.

rules.rule_name: New Jersey single-trip OS/OW permit is time- and movement-specific
rules.definition: A New Jersey single-trip oversize or overweight permit is valid for five days.

rules.rule_name: New Jersey Code 23 OS/OW permit is route-specific and non-divisible-load limited
rules.definition: A New Jersey Code 23 permit is route-specific.

rules.rule_name: New Jersey permit operation carries liability and insurance requirements
rules.definition: A New Jersey size or weight permit holder remains liable for injury or damage arising from the permitted operation as described in the guide.

rules.rule_name: New Jersey oversize permit movements are subject to time and holiday conditions
rules.definition: An oversize permit movement with less than 10 feet of clear space on the traveled way is limited to daylight operation under the guide's stated visibility condition.

structured_values.measurement_scope: clear traveled-way space for oversize permit movement

rules.rule_name: New Jersey OS/OW operation may require escorts, signs, lamps, reflective devices, and flags
rules.definition: A New Jersey oversize or overweight permit movement requires escort vehicles when the dimensions and conditions in the guide's escort tables are met.

rules.rule_name: Large trucks may detour only as necessary and must return to the designated network
rules.definition: A covered large truck may detour from an authorized route only as necessary to bypass a closure or restriction.

rules.rule_name: Terminal trips should avoid residential areas where feasible
rules.definition: To the extent feasible, a trip by the covered large-truck classes to a terminal should avoid residential areas.

rules.rule_name: NJ Access Network designation concerns width and does not guarantee unrestricted movement
rules.definition: Designation as a New Jersey Access Network route pertains to permissible width and does not guarantee free movement where route, bridge-weight, or vertical-clearance restrictions apply.

rules.rule_name: Terminal access follows the direct route and restricted roads only when they provide the only access
rules.definition: A covered large truck may use access-network and local unrestricted roads as necessary by the direct route.
source_sections: 16:32-1.5(a) and definition of direct route, PDF pages 4 and 6

rules.rule_name: NJDOT truck-network maps do not supersede regulatory text
rules.definition: Maps and graphic depictions of the designated truck network are not regulatory descriptions that supersede or replace the textual route descriptions adopted in the chapter.

rules.rule_name: PANYNJ truck-information snapshot lists a 4:00 p.m. APM OOG cutoff
rules.definition: The archived June 25, 2026 PANYNJ truck-information page lists a 4:00 p.m. gate cutoff for APM out-of-gauge loads.
source_sections: Gate Hours - APM Terminals, PDF page 4

structured_values.measurement_scope: APM out-of-gauge load cutoff in the archived PANYNJ truck-information snapshot

rules.rule_name: TWIC holders have continuing disclosure and surrender responsibilities
rules.definition: A TWIC applicant or holder has the continuing disclosure obligations specified in 49 CFR 1572.19. A TWIC holder must notify TSA immediately if the credential is lost, damaged, or stolen.

rules.rule_name: TWIC generally expires five years after issuance
rules.definition: A TWIC generally expires five years after issuance.

rules.rule_name: APM main intersection is one-way north-to-south
rules.definition: Beginning March 10, 2025, APM designates the main intersection after inbound as one-way from north to south.
source_sections: APM Mandatory Trucker Training and Safety Advisory, printed pages 20-21 / PDF page 12

rules.rule_name: Port guide prohibits queue jumping, blocking intersections, and U-turns
rules.definition: The PANYNJ truckers guide instructs drivers not to jump a vehicle queue.
source_sections: Obey and Follow the Rules of the Road, printed pages 4-5 / PDF page 4

rules.rule_name: NJ Turnpike left-lane restriction for heavy vehicles and trailers
rules.definition: On the Turnpike, a vehicle over 10,000 pounds GVWR or with an attached trailer or semitrailer may not use the farthest-left lane in a three-lane configuration, the two farthest-left lanes in a configuration of four or more lanes, or a lane designated Cars Only, except where posted or when a stated emergency or law-enforcement exception applies.
source_sections: N.J.A.C. 19:9-1.9(a), Traffic control on the Turnpike

rules.rule_name: US 1&9 speed limit at the North Avenue approach
rules.definition: The maximum legal speed is 40 mph in both directions on US 1&9 in Elizabeth between the Bayway traffic circle and 100 feet north of North Avenue, approximately mileposts 43.11 to 45.46.
source_sections: Union County, City of Elizabeth, Zone 2

rules.rule_name: US 1&9 no-stopping or standing zone at North Avenue
rules.definition: Stopping or standing is prohibited at all times along both sides of US 1&9 between Fairmount Avenue and a point 200 feet north of North Avenue.
source_sections: Union County, City of Elizabeth, no stopping or standing along both sides

rules.rule_name: No parking on North Avenue East from Route 1 to Division Street
rules.definition: Parking is prohibited at all times on both sides of North Avenue East from Route 1 to Division Street. Parking is prohibited at all times on both sides of McLester Street between Bay Avenue and Tripoli Street.

rules.rule_name: No stopping or standing on North Avenue East from Division Street to McLester Street
rules.definition: Stopping or standing is prohibited at any time on both sides of North Avenue East from Division Street to McLester Street. Stopping or standing is prohibited at any time on both sides of McLester Street from North Avenue East to Bay Avenue.

rules.rule_name: APM communicates closure appointment changes through e-alerts
rules.definition: APM states that it communicates appointment-availability changes caused by terminal closure through e-alerts.

rules.rule_name: RFID required on registered Class 8 drayage truck
rules.definition: A Class 8 drayage truck seeking entry to a Port of New York and New Jersey marine terminal must have a valid RFID tag properly mounted on the vehicle. Each RFID tag in the Drayage Truck Registry may be associated with only one unique vehicle.

rules.rule_name: Return from local terminal access by direct route
rules.definition: After using a local unrestricted roadway for terminal access, a covered large truck should return to the National Network or New Jersey Access Network by the direct route.

rules.rule_name: 102-inch width on truck networks
rules.definition: A commercial vehicle is limited to 102 inches in width on the National Network and New Jersey Access Routes.

structured_values.measurement_scope: National Network and New Jersey Access Routes

rules.rule_name: 48-foot trailer length on other routes
rules.definition: A trailer or semitrailer is limited to 48 feet on routes other than the National Network and access routes, subject to the guide's configuration conditions.

structured_values.measurement_scope: trailer or semitrailer on routes other than the National Network and access routes

rules.rule_name: Safety induction after new SeaLink number
rules.definition: The APM guidance states that a driver receiving a new SeaLink number must retake the safety induction.
source_sections: APM Mandatory Trucker Training, printed page 18 / PDF page 11

rules.rule_name: Elizabeth four-ton street-exclusion schedule
rules.definition: A truck over four tons gross weight may not use a street listed in Elizabeth's four-ton exclusion schedule. Elizabeth's scheduled four-ton truck exclusion does not apply when a truck is used for the pickup and delivery of materials on the listed street.

rules.rule_name: North Avenue East 80,000-pound-zone table entry
rules.definition: Elizabeth Code §10.16.050 contains a table row labeled an 80,000-pound overweight vehicle zone on North Avenue East beginning 440 feet east of Kapkowski Road and extending east 520 feet to the vacated portion of North Avenue East and its connection to the Port Authority overweight vehicle zone.
source_sections: Elizabeth Code §10.16.050, North Avenue East table row

structured_values.conversion_method: pounds multiplied by 0.45359237; rounded to 0.01 kg

rules.rule_name: North Avenue East no-stop row with blank hours
rules.definition: Elizabeth's no-stopping-or-standing schedule contains a North Avenue East row from the New Jersey Turnpike underpass to McLester Street whose hours field is blank. Stopping or standing is prohibited at any time on both sides of Kapkowski Road from North Avenue East south for 1,440 feet.
source_sections: Elizabeth Code Chapter 10.28, Schedule III row

rules.rule_name: Elizabeth North Avenue East Schedule II parking prohibition — north side
rules.definition: Elizabeth Schedule II prohibits parking on the north side of North Avenue East from Dowd Avenue to Spring Street on Thursday from 1:00 p.m. to 4:00 p.m. Elizabeth Schedule II prohibits parking on the south side of North Avenue East from Dowd Avenue to Spring Street on Tuesday from 1:00 p.m. to 4:00 p.m.

rules.rule_name: Elizabeth emergency no-parking declaration
rules.definition: Elizabeth may declare temporary emergency no-parking under the authorization and procedures stated in §10.28.090.
activation_conditions: an authorized emergency declaration is made
temporary signs are displayed
applicable prior notice is provided
state or county approval is obtained where the affected road requires it

rules.rule_name: Elizabeth overnight commercial-vehicle street parking
rules.definition: A commercial vehicle may not be parked on an Elizabeth street from 9:00 p.m. to 6:00 a.m. A truck tractor may not be parked on an Elizabeth street from 6:00 p.m. to 6:00 a.m. For Elizabeth's §10.40.020 parking restrictions, a described commercial motor vehicle or truck tractor need not be registered as a commercial motor vehicle or carry commercial motor-vehicle plates. Elizabeth's §10.40.020 commercial-vehicle and truck-tractor street-parking prohibitions do not apply to authorized emergency vehicles.

rules.rule_name: Elizabeth trailer street parking
rules.definition: A trailer, pole trailer, recreational vehicle, camper, or boat may not be parked on an Elizabeth street, whether attached to a towing vehicle or not. Elizabeth's §10.40.075 street-parking prohibition does not apply while the described vehicle is making a delivery to premises on that street. Elizabeth's §10.40.075 street-parking prohibition does not apply while the described vehicle is used in public-utility work. Elizabeth's §10.40.075 street-parking prohibition does not apply during temporary parking while the described vehicle is actively engaged in repair or maintenance. Elizabeth's §10.40.075 street-parking prohibition does not apply while the described vehicle is attending an emergency.

rules.rule_name: Elizabeth three-minute idling limit
rules.definition: A stationary motor vehicle may not idle for more than three consecutive minutes in Elizabeth. Elizabeth's three-minute stationary-motor-vehicle idling limit does not apply when the vehicle is stopped because of traffic. Elizabeth's stationary-motor-vehicle idling provision does not apply to a vehicle operating solely on electric power.

rules.rule_name: Elizabeth noisy-vehicle operation
rules.definition: Elizabeth prohibits use of an automobile, motorcycle, bus, truck, trailer, or other vehicle that is so out of repair, so loaded, or used in a manner that creates loud and unnecessary grating, rattling, grinding, clanging, or other annoying noise. The noisy loading or unloading activity described by Elizabeth §8.48.020 is prohibited in a residential area from 10:00 p.m. to 7:00 a.m., extending to 9:00 a.m. when the following day is Sunday or a legal holiday. A stationary motor vehicle whose manufacturer's gross weight exceeds 10,000 pounds, or its attached auxiliary equipment, may not operate for more than three minutes in any hour while on a public right-of-way in a residential district, in a designated quiet zone, or on private property in a residential, industrial, or business zone unless within a completely enclosed structure or adequately baffled.

rules.rule_name: Elizabeth temporary street closure
rules.definition: The Mayor may temporarily close an Elizabeth street only under the findings, regulation, warning-sign, and approval conditions stated in Chapter 10.20.
activation_conditions: Mayor finds closure necessary for safety, health, or welfare
a regulation is issued
warning signs are posted
approval of the New Jersey Commissioner of Transportation is obtained

rules.rule_name: Elizabeth bridge-strike liability
rules.definition: A person who causes a truck lacking sufficient clearance to pass under a bridge must reimburse all resulting City costs within ten days after notice.
activation_conditions: person causes a truck lacking sufficient clearance to go under a bridge
City provides notice of costs

rules.rule_name: Elizabeth work-zone traffic controls
rules.definition: Traffic-control devices for covered Elizabeth street work must conform to the Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices. A detour for covered Elizabeth street work requires approval by the Elizabeth Police Traffic Division. Covered Elizabeth street work is ordinarily limited to 9:00 a.m. through 4:00 p.m.

rules.rule_name: Elizabeth snow-covered parking prohibition — North Avenue
rules.definition: When North Avenue from Route No. 1 to Newark Avenue is snow-covered, parking is prohibited until the street is plowed sufficiently and parking will not interfere with traffic, subject to the required signs.
activation_conditions: North Avenue from Route No. 1 to Newark Avenue is snow-covered
required signs are in place
exceptions: The prohibition ends after sufficient plowing when parking will not interfere with traffic.

rules.rule_name: Elizabeth Ordinance 6290 Front Street four-ton exclusion
rules.definition: A truck over four tons gross weight is excluded from Front Street from the Elizabeth River crossing to Port Avenue.
activation_conditions: truck is on Front Street from the Elizabeth River crossing to Port Avenue
exceptions: The inherited exception applies to trucks used for the pickup and delivery of materials on that street.

structured_values.conversion_method: four U.S. short tons converted at 907.18474 kg per ton

rules.rule_name: Union County park-road four-ton exclusion
rules.definition: A truck over four tons gross weight may not use a Union County park-system road listed in Schedule VI. Union County's scheduled four-ton park-road exclusion does not apply to trucks used for the pickup and delivery of materials on the listed street.
source_sections: Laws of Union County §138-8 and Schedule VI

rules.rule_name: Union County truck-route schedule reserved
rules.definition: Union County Schedule VII, referenced by §138-9 for a system of truck routes, is expressly reserved and lists no truck-route streets in the January 2026 compilation. Union County §138-9 states that trucks with a combined vehicle-and-load weight over four tons are excluded from all streets except those forming the system of truck routes described in Schedule VII.
source_sections: Laws of Union County §138-9 and Schedule VII

rules.rule_name: Union County temporary emergency no-parking
rules.definition: Union County may impose temporary emergency no-parking under the declaration, notice, sign, and removal procedures stated in §§138-23 through 138-26.
activation_conditions: authorized emergency declaration is made
temporary signs are placed
required prior-vehicle notice is provided
vehicle-removal procedure is followed
sign-effectiveness conditions are satisfied

rules.rule_name: Union County sub-20-ton bridge signs
rules.definition: Union County must place a sign stating the designated carrying capacity at a bridge whose carrying capacity is less than 20 tons, with the weight designation established by Board resolution.
activation_conditions: bridge carrying capacity is less than 20 tons
Board resolution establishes the weight designation

structured_values.conversion_method: 20 U.S. short tons converted at 907.18474 kg per ton

rules.rule_name: CDL Group A definition
rules.definition: A combination vehicle is in CDL Group A when its gross combination weight rating or gross combination weight is 26,001 pounds or more, whichever is greater, and the towed unit has a gross vehicle weight rating or gross vehicle weight over 10,000 pounds, whichever is greater. A heavy straight vehicle is in CDL Group B when its gross vehicle weight rating or gross vehicle weight is 26,001 pounds or more, whichever is greater. A small vehicle that does not meet CDL Group A or B requirements is in Group C when it is designed to transport 16 or more passengers, including the driver. A vehicle of any size that does not meet CDL Group A or B requirements is in Group C when used to transport material required to be placarded under 49 CFR part 172, subpart F, or any quantity of a select agent or toxin listed in 42 CFR part 73.
source_sections: 49 CFR 383.5, definitions of Commercial motor vehicle (Group C) and Hazardous materials

rules.rule_name: Required commercial-driver tests
rules.definition: A person must not operate a commercial motor vehicle unless the person has taken and passed the knowledge and driving tests required by 49 CFR 383.23(a)(1). A person must not operate a commercial motor vehicle unless the person possesses the commercial learner's permit or commercial driver's license required by 49 CFR 383.23(a)(2), including the proper class and endorsements for the vehicle or cargo or passengers transported.

rules.rule_name: Motor carrier USDOT registration before operation
rules.definition: A motor carrier, hazardous-materials safety-permit applicant, or intermodal equipment provider subject to 49 CFR 390.19T must file the applicable identification report—Form MCS-150, MCS-150B, or MCS-150C—before beginning operations. A motor carrier subject to 49 CFR 390.19T must update its registration information every 24 months according to the USDOT-number schedule.

rules.rule_name: Carrier legal or trade name marking
rules.definition: A self-propelled commercial motor vehicle subject to 49 CFR 390.21T must display the motor carrier's legal name or single trade name on both sides. A self-propelled commercial motor vehicle subject to 49 CFR 390.21T must display the motor carrier's USDOT number preceded by the letters USDOT on both sides. A marking required by 49 CFR 390.21T must be readily legible during daylight from 50 feet while the vehicle is stationary.

rules.rule_name: Intermodal equipment provider inspection program
rules.definition: An intermodal equipment provider subject to 49 CFR 390.40T must systematically inspect, repair, and maintain intermodal equipment intended for interchange with a motor carrier.

rules.rule_name: Driver intermodal-equipment defect report
rules.definition: A driver or motor carrier transporting intermodal equipment must report known damage, defects, or deficiencies to the intermodal equipment provider or its designated agent when the equipment is returned, and the report must contain at least the items required by 49 CFR 396.11(b)(1).
source_sections: 49 CFR 390.42(b), incorporating the report items in 49 CFR 396.11(b)(1)
activation_conditions: damage, defects, or deficiencies are known when intermodal equipment is returned

rules.rule_name: Interstate commercial-motor-vehicle driver age
rules.definition: A driver subject to 49 CFR 391.11 must be at least 21 years old. A driver subject to 49 CFR 391.11 must, through experience, training, or both, be able to safely operate the type of commercial motor vehicle driven. A driver subject to 49 CFR 391.11 must possess a currently valid commercial motor vehicle operator's license issued by only one State or jurisdiction.

rules.rule_name: Driver medical certification and credential possession
rules.definition: A person subject to 49 CFR part 391 must not operate a commercial motor vehicle unless medically certified as physically qualified and, when on duty, carrying the required current medical examiner's certificate, subject to the CDL/CLP carrying exception and variance-document rules in 49 CFR 391.41(a)(1)-(2). A person is physically qualified to drive a commercial motor vehicle when the person meets the standards in 49 CFR 391.41(b) and the examination requirements in 49 CFR 391.43, or has the FMCSA medical variance described in 49 CFR 391.41(a)(3)(ii) and complies with §391.43.

rules.rule_name: Compliance with local laws
rules.definition: A commercial motor vehicle must be operated in accordance with the laws, ordinances, and regulations of the jurisdiction where it is being operated, subject to the stricter federal-rule condition in 49 CFR 392.2.

rules.rule_name: Driver equipment inspection before operation
rules.definition: A commercial motor vehicle may not be driven unless the driver is satisfied that the equipment specified in 49 CFR 392.7 is in good working order.

rules.rule_name: Cargo securement inspection before operation
rules.definition: A driver subject to 49 CFR 392.9 must be satisfied before driving that cargo is properly distributed and adequately secured.

rules.rule_name: Intermodal-container four-corner securement
rules.definition: An intermodal container carried on a container chassis must be secured to the chassis at all lower corners as specified by 49 CFR 393.126(b)(1). The securement devices for an intermodal container on a chassis must prevent more than 1.27 cm (1/2 inch) of movement relative to the chassis in the forward, aft, right, and left directions. The securement devices for an intermodal container on a chassis must prevent more than 2.54 cm (1 inch) of vertical movement relative to the chassis.

rules.rule_name: Eleven-hour driving limit
rules.definition: A property-carrying commercial motor vehicle driver subject to 49 CFR 395.3 may drive no more than 11 hours after 10 consecutive hours off duty. A property-carrying commercial motor vehicle driver subject to 49 CFR 395.3 may not drive after the end of the 14th consecutive hour after coming on duty following 10 consecutive hours off duty. A property-carrying commercial motor vehicle driver subject to 49 CFR 395.3 may not drive when more than eight hours of driving have passed without a consecutive 30-minute interruption made up of off-duty, sleeper-berth, or on-duty-not-driving time, or a consecutive combination of those periods.

rules.rule_name: Driver record of duty status
rules.definition: Except for a private motor carrier of passengers (nonbusiness), each driver subject to 49 CFR 395.8 must record duty status for each 24-hour period using the applicable method in 49 CFR 395.8(a)(1).
exceptions: private motor carrier of passengers (nonbusiness) exception in 49 CFR 395.8(a)(2)
ELD, manual record, time-record, and other method-specific provisions in 49 CFR 395.8 and 395.1 remain controlling

rules.rule_name: Electronic logging device use
rules.definition: A motor carrier required to use an electronic logging device must use only an ELD on FMCSA's registered-ELDs list.
activation_conditions: motor carrier is required to use an ELD under 49 CFR part 395
exceptions: regulatory exceptions in 49 CFR part 395 remain controlling

rules.rule_name: Systematic vehicle maintenance
rules.definition: A motor carrier subject to 49 CFR 396.3 must systematically inspect, repair, and maintain each vehicle under its control.

rules.rule_name: Driver vehicle inspection before driving
rules.definition: A driver subject to 49 CFR 396.13 must be satisfied that the motor vehicle is in safe operating condition before driving it.

rules.rule_name: Annual inspection recency condition
rules.definition: A motor carrier must not use a commercial motor vehicle, and an intermodal equipment provider must not tender equipment to a motor carrier, unless the vehicle or equipment has passed an inspection in accordance with 49 CFR 396.17 during the preceding 12 months. A motor carrier must not use a commercial motor vehicle, and an intermodal equipment provider must not tender equipment to a motor carrier, unless documentation of the most recent periodic inspection is on the vehicle.

rules.rule_name: Hazardous-material placarding
rules.definition: A transport vehicle containing hazardous material in a quantity and category specified by 49 CFR 172.504 must be placarded as required by that section.
activation_conditions: material, quantity, packaging, and table conditions in §172.504 are satisfied

rules.rule_name: Hazardous-material security-plan development
rules.definition: A person who offers for transportation or transports hazardous material listed in 49 CFR 172.800(b) must develop a transportation security plan meeting 49 CFR 172.802. A person who offers for transportation or transports hazardous material listed in 49 CFR 172.800(b) must adhere to the transportation security plan required by that section.

rules.rule_name: Placarded hazardous-material route selection
rules.definition: When a placarded or marked hazardous material is not subject to a prescribed or restricted NRHM routing designation, the motor vehicle must avoid routes through or near heavily populated areas, places where crowds are assembled, tunnels, narrow streets, and alleys, unless an alternative allowed by 49 CFR 397.67(b) applies.
activation_conditions: vehicle contains placarded or marked hazardous material
the material is not subject to a prescribed or restricted NRHM routing designation
exceptions: a reasonable deviation is necessary to reach a terminal, point of loading or unloading, facility for food, fuel, repairs, or rest, or a safe haven
an emergency, highway-authority direction, or law-enforcement direction requires a deviation

rules.rule_name: TWIC possession for unescorted secure-area access
rules.definition: A person seeking unescorted access to a secure area of a regulated vessel or facility must possess a TWIC unless an applicable regulatory exception applies.
activation_conditions: area is a secure area of a regulated vessel or facility
person seeks unescorted access

rules.rule_name: Escorted access without TWIC
rules.definition: A person not described in 33 CFR 101.514 must present compliant personal identification to gain entry to a regulated vessel or facility and must remain under escort while inside a secure area. Each person issued or possessing a TWIC must present the TWIC for inspection when requested by TSA, the Coast Guard, another authorized DHS representative, an authorized NTSB representative, or a Federal, State, or local law-enforcement officer. Each person issued or possessing a TWIC must pass an electronic TWIC inspection and submit a reference biometric and any other required information when requested by an official listed in 33 CFR 101.515(d)(2).

rules.rule_name: Conditional secure-area access for newly hired facility employees
rules.definition: A newly hired facility employee may be granted secure-area entry for up to 30 consecutive calendar days before receiving a TWIC only when the conditions in 33 CFR 105.257(b) are met, the employee is accompanied by a TWIC holder, the initial name check has passed, and the employee is not being hired as the Facility Security Officer or to perform facility-security duties. If TSA does not act on a newly hired facility employee's TWIC application within 30 days, the cognizant Coast Guard COTP may extend secure-area access for another 30 days.

rules.rule_name: UIIA premises access for equipment interchange
rules.definition: A participating provider or facility operator grants a participating motor carrier the right to enter its terminal facility solely to complete an interchange of equipment.
activation_conditions: the provider or facility operator and motor carrier are parties to the UIIA
entry is solely to complete an equipment interchange

rules.rule_name: UIIA good-cause premises-access refusal
rules.definition: A participating provider or facility operator may refuse a motor carrier access for good cause shown. A participating provider or facility operator must exercise its right to suspend a motor carrier's interchange privileges in good faith. A participating provider or facility operator must give the motor carrier advance notice of a pending suspension by e-mail through IANA. Advance notice of an interchange-privilege suspension must be furnished no less than three business days before the suspension becomes effective. A pending-suspension notice must include the reason for the action. A pending-suspension notice must include provider contact information needed to resolve the issue.

rules.rule_name: UIIA equipment-interchange receipt execution
rules.definition: At the time of interchange, the parties or their agents must execute an equipment-interchange receipt or exchange an electronic equivalent. The equipment-interchange receipt or electronic equivalent must describe the equipment and damage observable at the time of interchange.

rules.rule_name: UIIA FMCSR compliance before equipment interchange
rules.definition: UIIA parties must not interchange equipment unless they have complied with the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulations.
activation_conditions: an equipment interchange is proposed

rules.rule_name: UIIA motor-carrier pre-trip inspection
rules.definition: A motor carrier must conduct a pre-trip inspection that includes the Exhibit A items before departing with interchanged equipment.
source_sections: UIIA D.3.b and Exhibit A, PDF pages 6 and 22
activation_conditions: before departing with interchanged equipment

rules.rule_name: UIIA prompt equipment return
rules.definition: A motor carrier must promptly return interchanged equipment after its interchange purpose is complete.
activation_conditions: the purpose for which the equipment was interchanged is complete

rules.rule_name: UIIA changed return-location notice deadline
rules.definition: Whenever an equipment return location is changed, the provider must notify the motor carrier by e-mail by 16:00 local time on the business day before the change becomes effective. A motor carrier must return equipment to the physical location where it was received unless the provider directs return to a listed provider-designated satellite location within the same local commercial territory.

rules.rule_name: UIIA commercial automobile liability minimum
rules.definition: A participating motor carrier must maintain commercial automobile insurance with a combined single limit of $1,000,000 or greater.
activation_conditions: carrier participates under the UIIA

structured_values.measurement_scope: UIIA participating motor-carrier commercial automobile liability combined single limit

rules.rule_name: UIIA commercial general liability minimum
rules.definition: A participating motor carrier must maintain commercial general liability insurance with a combined single limit of $1,000,000 per occurrence or greater. No portion of the commercial general liability coverage required by UIIA F.6.b may be self-insured.

rules.rule_name: UIIA UIIE-1 insurance endorsement
rules.definition: A participating motor carrier must keep a UIIE-1 endorsement, or a corresponding form that does not differ from UIIE-1, in the most current form available attached to its commercial automobile liability policy. The motor carrier's insurance company must provide IANA evidence of the endorsement and coverage required by UIIA F.6.c.

rules.rule_name: APM driver location instruction
rules.definition: APM's live Port Status page instructs drivers to remain in their trucks unless in designated safe areas. APM's live Port Status page instructs that a single RFID tag be mounted on the exterior of the truck, specifically the mirror bracket.
source_sections: Port Status page, undated Safety Information

rules.rule_name: APM export appointment horizon
rules.definition: APM's live Port Status page states that export drop-off appointments may be booked up to two working days in advance. APM's live Port Status page instructs drivers to have a ticket showing COMPLETE before exiting the terminal. APM's live Port Status page instructs drivers to merge appointments before entering the OCR sheds at pre-gate. APM's live Port Status page states that appointments cannot be managed after the one-hour appointment window. APM's live Port Status page instructs drivers to check container status before booking import pickup appointments.
source_sections: Port Status page, undated Gate Information

rules.rule_name: Union County traffic-ordinance responsibility statement
rules.definition: Union County §133-10(A) states that responsibility for traffic regulation on County roads rests with Union County. Under Union County §133-10(B)-(C), when a municipality adopts a traffic ordinance affecting a County road, the County's stated policy is to adopt a consenting resolution.

rules.rule_name: Union County road-sign allocation — municipal signs
rules.definition: Union County §133-14 assigns municipalities responsibility for installing regulatory signs and school-warning signs on County roads. Union County §133-14 assigns the County responsibility for directional and other warning signs on County roads, with municipal consent.

rules.rule_name: Union County planning-table truck-route label
rules.definition: Union County's Safe Streets for All Appendix G labels North Avenue between NJ 27 and U.S. 1 and 9 in Elizabeth, mileposts 0.00 through 0.67, as Truck Route: Yes.
source_sections: Appendix G, printed page 23, North Avenue corridor row

structured_values.measurement_scope: North Avenue between NJ 27 and U.S. 1 and 9

rules.rule_name: Elizabeth Ordinance 6096 notice description
rules.definition: Elizabeth's official final-reading notice describes Ordinance 6096 as replacing a $250 maximum penalty with a $250 minimum penalty for off-street parking of commercial vehicles in residential zones.

structured_values.measurement_scope: off-street commercial-vehicle parking in residential zones as described by the official notice
former off-street commercial-vehicle parking penalty described by the official notice

rules.rule_name: Elizabeth Chapter 10.40 minimum penalty
rules.definition: Unless another New Jersey statute or another section of Chapter 10.40 expressly provides a different penalty, a person convicted of a Chapter 10.40 violation is liable to a penalty of not less than $250. For a Chapter 10.40 violation, §10.40.050 permits imprisonment for a term not exceeding 15 days, or both imprisonment and the stated monetary penalty.
